question: The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers ________ percent of human history.
solution:
The correct answer is __**99**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic.
 
• This long span of time covers 99% of human history
 
• Archaeologists have given lengthy names for the time that we are studying.
 
• They call the earliest period the Palaeolithic. This comes from two Greek words, ‘palaeo’, meaning old, and ‘lithos’, meaning stone.
 
• The name points to the importance of finds of stone tools.
 
• The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago.
 
• This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic.
 
• The Palaeolithic cultures flourished in the geological era called the Pleistocene.
 
• In this period Homo erectus first time used fire, made stone tools and other implements, 
 
 
• and used the clean skin of other animals therefore may be taken to represent the beginning of true man. 
 
 
 
• The Pleistocene era, climatically, is characterised by glacial (extreme cold conditions and extensive ice caps) and interglacial (warm period) conditions in the temperate zones and pluvial (heavy rainy or wet period) and interpluvial (dry period) conditions in the tropical belt.
 
• Early human populations (i.e. Palaeolithic) lived in major parts of the temperate zones (Europe) and tropical zones (Africa and Asia) successfully adapting to these climatic events and environments.
 
• Evidence of fire in the form of a hearth is known from Upper Palaeolithic caves in the Kurnool area and is dated to about 16,000 years ago.
